title: Unable to sync from Android to macos
body:
### What happened?

```
Puller (folder "redmi11" (transport), item "130.jpg"): syncing: finishing: pull: generic error
2024/10/18 07:48:49 INFO: "redmi11" (transport): Failed to sync 81 items
2024/10/18 07:48:49 INFO: Folder "redmi11" (transport) isn't making sync progress - retrying in 1m1s.
```

Suddenly became abnormal, likely because I updated the macOS version yesterday. Now macOS is using the latest v1.28.0, macOS (64-bit Intel/AMD), while Android is using v1.27.12(Downloaded from F-Droid). Currently, all synchronized folders, which I confirmed have not been modified and were previously working normally, are set to 'Send and Receive' on both ends. However, the reality is that only changes from macOS can be synchronized to Android, while changes from Android cannot be synchronized to macOS (it seems that only delete operations can be synchronized, but I have all the necessary permissions and it used to work normally). If changes are made on the Android side in the corresponding synchronized folder, a hidden file like '.syncthing.130.jpg.tmp' (and the size of this file seems to be the same as the original file) is generated on the macOS side, and it shows 'Unsynced'.

Could it be due to the difference in major versions?

### Syncthing version

macos v1.28.0 - android v1.27.12

### Platform & operating system

macos 11.7.10 - android 13 (redmi miui14)

### Browser version

Safari v16.6.1 (16615.3.12.11.5, 16615)

### Relevant log output

```shell
[NGSNT] 2024/10/18 08:05:18 INFO: Puller (folder "redmi11" (transport), item "130.jpg"): syncing: finishing: pull: generic error
[NGSNT] 2024/10/18 08:05:18 INFO: "redmi11" (transport): Failed to sync 81 items
[NGSNT] 2024/10/18 08:05:18 INFO: Folder "redmi11" (transport) isn't making sync progress - retrying in 16m1s.
[NGSNT] 2024/10/18 08:06:09 INFO: Puller (folder "redmi" (tran), item "test.txt"): syncing: finishing: pull: generic error
[NGSNT] 2024/10/18 08:06:09 INFO: "redmi11" (transfer): Failed to sync 1 items
[NGSNT] 2024/10/18 08:06:09 INFO: Folder "music_transfer" (music_transfer) isn't making sync progress - retrying in 1m0s.
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: ”Generic error” there basically means the source (Android) couldn’t find or read the file. I don’t think it’s related to a macOS update.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I don't want to jump to conclusions, but I suspect the issue might be related to the update of Syncthing from version 1.27.x to 1.28.0. My two Android phones are still able to sync normally with each other, but the problem is that my phone can no longer sync to my computer. Everything was working fine yesterday morning, but in the afternoon, I updated the Syncthing version on my macOS to 1.28.0. Then, in the evening, I discovered that I could no longer sync from my Android to my macOS.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: This needs troubleshooting, screenshots, logs, experimentation, whatnot, so I suggest you open a thread on the forum. Once the problem is understood and actionable it can be solved here.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Thank you for your help. As I mentioned in https://<redacted-host>/t/export-settings/22984, everything is back to normal after downgrading the version. Yesterday, after the upgrade, the Syncthing version on my macOS was 1.28.x. In the past, I had also experienced different versions of Syncthing on macOS and my phones, but the versions were all within 1.27.x, and there were no issues. So, this time, I suspect the problem was due to the major version 1.28.x (28) exceeding the 1.27.x (27) on my Android phones. Otherwise, it might be an issue with my computer. Fortunately, after downgrading the version, everything is back to normal, and it's as smooth as before, haha.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I tested it myself a bit, and it's strange that it wasn't completely non-functional at the time. It could only sync in one direction (from macOS to Android phones), which worked fine in that direction. However, after making changes in the sync folder on the Android phone, it couldn't sync back to macOS. This direction just didn't work, and it kept generating some hidden files with the same size as the files on the phone, named in the way I mentioned before, like '.syncthing.fileName.suffix.tmp'.

When I ran both on 1.27.x instead, it synced fine.

Updating the Android device to version 1.28.0 results in the same permanent issue despite receiving devices using 1.28.0 and 1.27.12 being available.

I used the update distributed on F-Droid in the hopes it fixes this issue but this was not the case and rather resulted in spending too much time to undo the update and redo all settings.
